CALL_BY_NAME.label: Call by name
CALL_BY_NAME.description: Arguments are evaluated only when needed

identity-function.label: Identity Function
identity-function.description: the simplest possible term — apply λx:T.x to a variable a:T and get a back unchanged

type-alias-basic-synonym.label: Type Alias: Basic Synonym
type-alias-basic-synonym.description: typedef X = T introduces a transparent synonym, usable anywhere T could be

type-alias-chained.label: Type Alias: Chained
type-alias-chained.description: a typedef built from an earlier typedef resolves through the whole chain to Nat

type-alias-function-type.label: Type Alias: Function Type
type-alias-function-type.description: aliasing a compound (arrow) type to shorten a repeated signature

application-chain-compose-twice.label: Application Chain: compose & twice
application-chain-compose-twice.description: identity, compose, and twice combined — twice applies (compose identity identity) to itself, a classic higher-order-function workout

alpha-conversion.label: Alpha Conversion
alpha-conversion.description: the outer y (bound outside) is shadowed by the inner λy — the body's x still refers to the outer parameter, unaffected by the name clash

booleans-if.label: Booleans & If
booleans-if.description: if/then/elseif/else chain over Bool — the first true branch wins (elseif true then 200 short-circuits before else)

ascription-sequencing.label: Ascription & Sequencing
ascription-sequencing.description: unit; 42 sequences a Unit-typed effect then a Nat result, and the whole thing is ascribed to Nat

dummy-abstraction.label: Dummy Abstraction: λ_
dummy-abstraction.description: λ_:T.t discards its argument entirely — the parameter is never given a name, so it can't be referenced in the body

arithmetic.label: Arithmetic
arithmetic.description: + - * / over Nat — all four share one precedence level (left-to-right), so group with parens to control order

comparison.label: Comparison
comparison.description: < <= > >= == != over Nat, each producing a Bool usable directly in an if

church-booleans-pairs.label: Church Booleans & Pairs
church-booleans-pairs.description: tru/fls encode booleans as pure functions (no Bool type at all), pair/fst/snd encode a 2-tuple the same way — fst (pair tru fls) reduces to tru; enable the Untyped lambda calculus theory

church-booleans-and-or-not.label: Church Booleans: and / or / not
church-booleans-and-or-not.description: and/or/not built from tru/fls as selectors — (tru and fls) or (not fls) reduces to tru

church-booleans-if-test.label: Church Booleans: if (test)
church-booleans-if-test.description: test b c a picks c if b is true, a if false — exactly what applying a Church boolean directly already does; test just names it

church-numerals-zero-succ-numbers.label: Church Numerals: Zero, Succ, Numbers
church-numerals-zero-succ-numbers.description: a numeral n means "apply s to z, n times" — three succ zero unfolds it back into 3 nested succ calls

church-numerals-the-core-idea-repeat-n-t.label: Church Numerals: The Core Idea (Repeat N Times)
church-numerals-the-core-idea-repeat-n-t.description: a numeral n is really a generic "apply f to x, n times" machine — three not fls flips fls three times, landing on tru

church-arithmetic-addition-plus.label: Church Arithmetic: Addition (plus)
church-arithmetic-addition-plus.description: plus applies s, m times then n times, on top of z — (plus two three) succ zero unfolds to 5 nested succs

church-arithmetic-multiplication-times.label: Church Arithmetic: Multiplication (times)
church-arithmetic-multiplication-times.description: times adds n to zero, m times over — m × n by repeated addition; (times two three) succ zero unfolds to 6

church-numerals-iszero.label: Church Numerals: iszero
church-numerals-iszero.description: n (λx.fls) tru applies always-false to tru, n times — survives unchanged only when n never applies it, i.e. n = zero

church-numerals-predecessor-pred.label: Church Numerals: Predecessor (pred)
church-numerals-predecessor-pred.description: Church numerals have no built-in predecessor — runs a (prev, current) pair forward n times from (0,0), landing on (n-1, n)

y-combinator-never-terminates.label: Y Combinator: Never Terminates
y-combinator-never-terminates.description: x x applies x to itself — impossible in any typed fragment above. Y id diverges under every strategy here, just differently: grows forever under Call-by-value, cycles forever under Normal order/Call-by-name — see the fixx example for the fix

fixx-the-call-by-value-safe-fix.label: fixx: The Call-by-value-safe Fix
fixx-the-call-by-value-safe-fix.description: same self-application as Y, but the extra λy defers it until needed — fixx id settles to a value under Call-by-value/Call-by-name instead of diverging (Normal order still unfolds forever). Called "fixx" here — plain "fix" is already a reserved builtin

fixx-real-recursion-iseven.label: fixx: Real Recursion (isEven)
fixx-real-recursion-iseven.description: Y/fixx used for real: isEvenGen recurses through f. Scott-encoded naturals keep pred/iszero cheap; both branches are thunked so Call-by-value isn't too eager — isEven three reduces to fls

sum-types-inl-inr.label: Sum Types: inl / inr
sum-types-inl-inr.description: inl 5 : Nat+Bool builds the left alternative; case ... of inl x => ... || inr y => ... recovers it, picking the Nat branch

variants-labeled-sum.label: Variants: Labeled Sum
variants-labeled-sum.description: an n-ary labeled sum type ([circle:Nat, square:Nat]) generalizing binary inl/inr — matched with case ... of [label=x] => ...

enums-via-variants-traffic-light.label: Enums via Variants (Traffic Light)
enums-via-variants-traffic-light.description: an enum is just a variant where every case carries the same (often trivial) payload — next cycles red -> green -> yellow -> red by case matching

optional-maybe-via-sum-types.label: Optional (Maybe) via Sum Types
optional-maybe-via-sum-types.description: Nat+Unit encodes Option Nat — inl n is Some n, inr unit is None; getOrElse none 42 falls back to the default since there's nothing to unwrap

tuples.label: Tuples
tuples.description: a heterogeneous tuple literal <1, true, 2>, projected positionally with .2

records.label: Records
records.description: a labeled record literal <name=1, flag=true>, projected by field name with .flag

chained-projections.label: Chained Projections
chained-projections.description: projecting through a function's result (swap<7,9>).1, plus a tuple-inside-a-record chain .2.label

head-of-a-list.label: Head of a List
head-of-a-list.description: cons/nil construction, then head extracts the first element — the lecture's own worked example (reduces to 3)

isnil-empty-vs-non-empty.label: isnil: Empty vs. Non-empty
isnil-empty-vs-non-empty.description: isnil[Nat] tests whether a list is nil — here on a non-empty list (cons 1 nil), so it reduces to false

tail-drop-the-first-element.label: tail: Drop the First Element
tail-drop-the-first-element.description: tail[Nat] on a two-element list (cons 1 (cons 2 nil)) drops the head, leaving cons[Nat] 2 nil[Nat]

nat-via-the-lecture-s-own-definition.label: Nat via μ: the lecture's own definition
nat-via-the-lecture-s-own-definition.description: NatRec ≅ μX.[zero:Unit, succ:X] — exactly the lecture's "Nat = μX..." (renamed NatRec here since Nat itself is reserved for the language's built-in numeral literals); defines zero/succ/iszero/pred, then checks iszero(zero)

nat-via-iszero-succ-zero-false.label: Nat via μ: iszero(succ zero) = false
nat-via-iszero-succ-zero-false.description: same NatRec encoding — unfold exposes the variant so iszero's case-split lands on the "succ" branch instead of "zero"

nat-via-pred-succ-n-n.label: Nat via μ: pred(succ n) = n
nat-via-pred-succ-n-n.description: pred unfolds one succ-cell and hands back its payload directly, undoing the succ that was just applied

nat-via-pred-zero-zero.label: Nat via μ: pred(zero) = zero
nat-via-pred-zero-zero.description: the usual boundary convention — pred of zero is defined to just hand back zero again, rather than being left stuck

fold-unfold-cancellation-e-unfoldfold.label: fold/unfold cancellation (E-unfoldfold)
fold-unfold-cancellation-e-unfoldfold.description: unfold[T](fold[T] v) → v in a single evaluation step — the core isomorphism rule, isolated from the Nat encoding so it's visible on its own

over-a-function-type.label: μ over a function type
over-a-function-type.description: recursive types aren't limited to variant/record bodies — μX.(X→X) is a self-referential function type, folded and unfolded exactly the same way

factorial-via-fix.label: Factorial via fix
factorial-via-fix.description: the classic fix g factorial encoding, g : (Nat->Nat)->Nat->Nat — g's own recursive call goes through the fixpoint operator instead of naming itself

fibonacci-via-fix.label: Fibonacci via fix
fibonacci-via-fix.description: same fixpoint pattern as factorial, but with two recursive calls per step, g : (Nat->Nat)->Nat->Nat

non-terminating-fix.label: Non-terminating fix
non-terminating-fix.description: fix (λx:Nat.x) unfolds to itself forever with no base case — hits the evaluator's step limit rather than a value

let-bindings.label: Let Bindings
let-bindings.description: bind a name with let x = ..., then reference it in the body — no polymorphism needed for a single monomorphic use

let-bound-function.label: Let-bound Function
let-bound-function.description: bind an unannotated function with let, then apply it in the body — its parameter type is inferred from the call site

nested-let-shadowing.label: Nested Let: Shadowing
nested-let-shadowing.description: an inner let x = true shadows the outer let x = 1 within its own body, without affecting the outer binding

let-polymorphism-id-at-two-types.label: Let-polymorphism: id at Two Types
let-polymorphism-id-at-two-types.description: id is generalized (∀A. A -> A) so the SAME definition is reused at Nat and Bool within one body — this needs the Let-polymorphism theory, not just Type inference

let-polymorphism-const.label: Let-polymorphism: const
let-polymorphism-const.description: const is generalized over two independent type variables (∀A,B. A -> B -> A) and reused at two different instantiations

type-inference-unannotated.label: Type Inference: Unannotated λ
type-inference-unannotated.description: with the Type inference theory on, an unannotated λx.x works even outside a let-bound value

type-inference-inferred-from-usage.label: Type Inference: Inferred from Usage
type-inference-inferred-from-usage.description: with Type inference on, f's parameter type is inferred from how f is applied inside the body (f 5 forces Nat), not from an explicit annotation

polymorphic-identity-system-f.label: Polymorphic Identity (System F)
polymorphic-identity-system-f.description: explicit type abstraction ΛX.λx:X.x : ∀X.X->X, instantiated explicitly at Nat and Bool via id[Nat]/id[Bool] — enable the System F theory

polymorphic-compose-system-f.label: Polymorphic Compose (System F)
polymorphic-compose-system-f.description: compose takes three explicit type parameters ∀A.∀B.∀C, instantiated with compose[Nat][Nat][Bool] to compose isZero after inc

identity-constructor-system-f.label: Identity Constructor (System Fω)
identity-constructor-system-f.description: typedef Id = λX:@.X — a type constructor of kind @→@ that's a no-op on types; (Id Nat) normalizes to Nat — enable the System Fω theory

endo-constructor-system-f.label: Endo Constructor (System Fω)
endo-constructor-system-f.description: typedef Endo = λX:@.X->X builds "the type of endofunctions on T" from any T, itself classified by kind @→@

dependent-head-system-p.label: Dependent Head (System λP)
dependent-head-system-p.description: typedef Vec : Nat -> @ declares an opaque, term-indexed type family; vecHead's Πn:Nat.Vec[n]->Nat type instantiates its own argument's expected type per call — enable the System λP theory

dependent-head-index-mismatch-system-p.label: Dependent Head: Index Mismatch (System λP)
dependent-head-index-mismatch-system-p.description: same head as above, but v4 : Vec[4] is passed where Vec[3] is expected — rejected because the index is baked into the type itself, not just a runtime value

extensions.heading: Active extensions
extensions.stlcDescription: Always on — the base type theory

letPolymorphism.label: Let-polymorphism
letPolymorphism.description: Reuse a let-bound value at several types (Hindley–Milner)

typeInference.label: Type inference
typeInference.description: Omit a λ's parameter type — it's inferred from use

isoRecursiveTypes.label: Iso-recursive types (μ)
isoRecursiveTypes.description: Self-referential types μX.T, via explicit fold / unfold

systemF.label: System F
systemF.description: Explicit polymorphism: ΛX. t and t [T]

systemFOmega.label: System Fω (type constructors)
systemFOmega.description: Type constructors: λX:@. T and F T, classified by kinds

systemLambdaP.label: System λP (dependent types)
systemLambdaP.description: Types that depend on terms: Π-types and Vec[n]-style indexing

untyped.label: Untyped lambda calculus
untyped.description: Only variables, abstraction, and application — everything else is rejected. Disables every other extension.

proofTree.logicUnavailableNonStlc: This term uses rules outside plain STLC, so it has no clean Curry-Howard reading
proofTree.logicUnavailableExtensions: Only available for plain STLC — turn off the active type system extensions to use it
proofTree.buildCheckUnavailableUntyped: Not available for untyped lambda calculus — there are no typing rules to build a derivation from
proofTree.showInferenceStepsTooltip: The derivation is shown before its constraints are solved. Turn this on to watch them being solved, step by step.
proofTree.clickToApplyStep: Click to jump to right after this constraint is solved
proofTree.clickToUndoStep: Click again to go back to right before this constraint
proofTree.noNewBindings: No new bindings — already consistent with what's known
proofTree.empty: Type a valid expression to generate a proof tree.
proofTree.emptyUntyped: Untyped lambda calculus has no type derivation to show.
proofTree.logicEmpty: This proof uses rules outside plain STLC, so it has no clean Curry-Howard reading.

proofBuilder.emptyNeedsTerm: Type a valid expression first — Practice needs a term that already type-checks.
proofBuilder.emptyHasErrors: This term doesn't type-check yet — fix the errors first, then come back to build its proof yourself.
proofBuilder.emptyInstructions: Construct the typing derivation for the current term yourself, then check it against the real one.
proofBuilder.contextQuestion: What gets added to the context here?
proofBuilder.turnIntoArrow: Turn this into an arrow type (wraps it as the left side, e.g. T → ?)
proofBuilder.constraintsQuestion: Which constraints does this judgement carry?
proofBuilder.constraintsHint: C is the union of the premises' constraint sets plus the equations this rule adds itself (e.g. CT-App adds T₁ = T₂ → X). Use ∅ if there are none.
proofBuilder.instantiateHint: Instantiate: replace every ∀-bound variable of the scheme in Γ with a fresh type variable, then write the resulting type.
proofBuilder.generalizeHint: Quantify (∀) the type variables that are free in the value's type but not free in Γ. Write the resulting type scheme.
proofBuilder.freshVariableHint: This λ has no parameter annotation, so its parameter gets a fresh type variable (e.g. X) — use that variable in the type.
proofBuilder.modeSemiHint: Click-to-build: pick rules and fill guided slots — the tree's shape is given
proofBuilder.modeManualHint: Type every judgement yourself and decide how many premises each rule has

latexExport.previewDescription: Standalone document using the ebproof package — matches exactly what's expanded or collapsed on screen right now.

home.heroLead: An interactive environment for experimenting with lambda calculus — typed and untyped — as this web playground and as a VS Code extension bringing the same views into your editor. It supports parsing, AST inspection/editing, type checking and inference, proof tree visualization, and building your own derivations by hand.
home.heroSub: Built as a Master Thesis project, the goal is to make the underlying theory explorable: you can see the syntax tree, derived types, and the proof steps that justify them.
home.overviewSubtitle: A type theory playground for learning, debugging, and research — in the browser or in VS Code

typeChecking.title: Type checking
typeChecking.description: Checks expressions using Simply Typed Lambda Calculus rules and produces structured errors.

typeInference.title: Type inference (HM)
typeInference.description: Infers principal types where possible, so you can experiment without annotations.

evaluation.title: Evaluation
evaluation.description: Reduces lambda terms under normal-order, call-by-value, or call-by-name strategies, with a step-by-step viewer and Γ bindings panel.

proofTree.title: Proof tree visualization
proofTree.description: Shows derivation trees step-by-step, making typing rules and contexts explicit.

ast.title: AST views & editing
ast.description: Inspect and (optionally) edit the AST in a structured form to avoid syntax errors.

synchronized.title: Multiple synchronized representations
synchronized.description: Text/AST/proof views are designed to represent the same underlying term.

exercises.title: Practice exercises
exercises.description: Construct a typing derivation yourself, rule by rule, and check it against the real answer with mistake highlighting.

theories.title: Extended type theories
theories.description: Toggle let-polymorphism, iso-recursive types, System F, System Fω, and dependent types (λP) on top of base STLC.

curryHoward.title: Curry–Howard / logic view
curryHoward.description: Re-renders an STLC typing derivation as a natural-deduction proof, with implication, conjunction, and disjunction rules.

latex.title: LaTeX / ebproof export
latex.description: Preview, copy, or download any proof tree as a ready-to-compile ebproof LaTeX document, matching what's on screen.

home.exploreLead: Short, hands-on pages that pair the theory with things to try in the editor.

msg.ruleMissing: Write the rule name (e.g. T-App or CT-Var).
msg.ruleMismatch: This rule doesn't fit this term.
msg.termMismatch: This isn't the sub-term this premise should derive.
msg.gammaExtra: Γ has bindings that don't belong here: {{names}}.
msg.gammaTypes: Γ has the right variables, but a type differs (or a variable name is reused inconsistently).
msg.typeMismatch: The type doesn't match this rule's conclusion.
msg.constraintsMismatch: C doesn't match: expected {{expected}} equation(s), found {{written}}. Remember C = the premises' constraints plus what this rule adds.
msg.premiseCount: This rule needs {{expected}} premise(s) here, you have {{written}}.
msg.expectedSideCondition: A side condition (membership, instantiate or generalize) belongs here, not a judgement.
msg.expectedJudgement: A full judgement belongs here, not a side condition.
msg.factForm: A different kind of side condition is needed here.
msg.constraintsRequired: This rule carries a constraint set C — add it.
msg.constraintsNotExpected: This rule has no constraint set — remove C.

manualBuilder.removeConstraints: Remove the constraint set from this judgement
manualBuilder.addConstraints: Add a constraint set C to this judgement
manualBuilder.constraintsPlaceholder: Write C₁, C₂ … for a premise's set, or define C_n in the Definitions box (a definition wins).
manualBuilder.definitionsHint: Name a set once and reuse it: one definition per line, like Γ_1 = {x : 'A} or C_1 = {…}. Then write Γ_1 or C_1 in any field. A plain Γ still means the parent's context.

evalPractice.finishedNormalForm: Normal form reached — nothing can be reduced any further.
evalPractice.finishedStuck: The evaluation is stuck here — no rule applies, but the term isn't a value.
evalPractice.finishedLimit: The trace stops at the step limit — the term may reduce further.

hint.NORMAL: Normal order reduces the leftmost, outermost redex, and it also reduces under a λ.
hint.CALL_BY_NAME: Call by name reduces the leftmost, outermost redex, but never under a λ, and it doesn't evaluate arguments first.
hint.CALL_BY_VALUE: Call by value reduces the function, then the argument, to values before applying it, and never under a λ.

msg.pickWrong: That isn't the sub-term reduced next.
msg.writeParse: Couldn't read that as a term: {{detail}}
msg.writeWrong: That's not what this sub-term reduces to. Substitute the argument for the parameter in the body (bound variables may be renamed).

evalPractice.emptyNeedsEvaluation: Evaluate an expression first — Practice needs a reduction to check your work against.
evalPractice.instruction: Work out the next {{strategy}} step: write what the next redex reduces to. Click a part of the term to select it (Shift+click inserts it right away); selecting the redex and checking are optional.
evalPractice.summary: {{correct}} of {{total}} steps matched the real reduction.
evalPractice.writeHint: Checking is optional — press Enter or Check to see how you're doing, or just go on. You can write the reduced sub-term or the whole next term.
